results.notes: Outcome column Overall; Day == 2. Individual randomized AI-design comparison. Source counts reproduced from PDF p. 21; coefficient and SE from Table S7, PDF p. 51. The extra regression-rating count is printed in the deposited Supplementary Material notebook, zero-based cell 22, not in the paper. Its text identifies conventional, nonrobust OLS; all three treatment arms enter the reproduction model. Complete cases for DAT, Experience, Ability and English: 267 writers and 1,068 ratings across three arms. Four Day 2 writers are omitted for missing baseline covariates (three Human Confirmation, one Human Creativity). Observed writer counts in that model: {"Copilot": 90, "Human Confirmation": 85, "Human Creativity": 92}. Arm-specific people counts are not printed in the paper. Each writer has one Day 2 story with four ratings. Average the four ratings by ID first; then compute means and sample SDs (ddof=1). The new difference is the unadjusted participant mean for the listed treatment minus the listed control within this model's analysis sample. HC2 comes from OLS with only an intercept and the pairwise arm indicator. Thus the new difference is not the paper's covariate-adjusted coefficient. Printed-coefficient orientation is preserved only in reproduced, and corrected to treatment minus control in computed. No cluster randomization is reported. Round all denotes the Day 2 between-person contrast; the fixed-order Day 1 baseline is excluded and supplies no paired or first-round estimate.

PDF p. 7; original 3large_result_df_A/B/C.csv embeddings and exact saved story texts; A = Human Creativity, B = Human Confirmation, C = Copilot as mapped in the Figure 4 notebook, zero-based cell 8 (read as text). Use the authors' saved 3,072-dimensional text-embedding-3-large vectors; no model substitution or new API call. Every story text matches its genre file. Recompute cosine similarity to the full within-arm mean embedding. This reproduces every saved Similarity value to floating-point precision (maximum errors 5.55e-16 and 7.77e-16) and all published means/CIs. The notebook plots saved Similarity and uses t intervals over stories. METHOD DISCREPANCY: the Figure 4C caption on PDF p. 16 says the average of other stories. Excluding each focal story instead gives treatment/control means 0.702021511789/0.736527840166, which do not match. The exact saved-output reproduction establishes that the published values use a self-inclusive centroid. This is disclosed rather than silently adopting the caption's different procedure. The protocol supplies one final story per writer on Day 2 (PDF pp. 4, 19); people counts therefore use one writer per story row, not rating or pair counts. The content files have no participant-ID linkage to the ratings CSV. Their Day 2 corpus has Human Creativity 93, Human Confirmation 91 and Copilot 91 stories (275 total), whereas the ratings file/paper's evaluated corpus has 93, 88 and 90 (271 total). These are distinct analysis pools; no invented cross-file exclusions are applied. The printed content arm means and CIs reproduce using the content corpus. Arm-specific content counts are not printed, so no unavailable count benchmark is asserted to match. Rule 5: retain only the original-unit set measure and raw difference (treatment minus control; higher means more similar). Shared centroids create dependence. No participant-level SD, HC2/paired/cluster SE or standardized effect is supplied; those fields, including se_type, are null.

PDF p. 6; authors' Figure 4 notebook zero-based cells 4 and 6, read as text. All unordered distinct-story pairs of the original nine binary genre vectors are compared by cosine similarity. A zero vector gives similarity zero. This exactly reproduces the published means and t CIs; treatment/control pair counts are 4278/4095. METHOD DISCREPANCY: the Figure 4B caption on PDF p. 16 describes similarity to the average of other stories, which is not what the supplied code computes. That caption formula instead gives treatment/control means 0.726521793227/0.722993524659 using the same zero-vector convention. The result here retains the exactly reproducible procedure that generated the published numbers, not the conflicting caption formula. The protocol supplies one final story per writer on Day 2 (PDF pp. 4, 19); people counts therefore use one writer per story row, not rating or pair counts. The content files have no participant-ID linkage to the ratings CSV. Their Day 2 corpus has Human Creativity 93, Human Confirmation 91 and Copilot 91 stories (275 total), whereas the ratings file/paper's evaluated corpus has 93, 88 and 90 (271 total). These are distinct analysis pools; no invented cross-file exclusions are applied. The printed content arm means and CIs reproduce using the content corpus. Arm-specific content counts are not printed, so no unavailable count benchmark is asserted to match. Rule 5: these are set-defined diversity measures. Arm SDs, difference SE and se_type are null; pairwise observations are not independent people. The reproduced published CIs treat pairs as observations and are not new participant-level precision. The difference is only the raw difference between the two set summaries; higher values mean more similarity.
